For LLMs, the most directly relevant papers say synthetic data curation works best when it accounts for interactions among samples, not just each sample in isolation. One paper argues that effective synthetic data curation requires group-level signals because individual-level signals can miss how dataset composition affects training; group-level curation improves downstream performance, especially generative capability, and matters more as pipelines become increasingly synthetic [1]. Another paper argues for online curation during training: ADAPT dynamically reweights samples based on quality signals and consistently beats offline selection and mixing under equal FLOPs [3].

Related papers cover specific curation settings. A bilevel fine-tuning framework combines offline selection with online self-refining generation to improve SFT data quality and downstream performance [9]. For synthetic dataset creation, AutoSynth automates workflow optimization for high-quality generation without reference datasets [4]. In recommendation, a layered, curated synthetic curriculum enables robust scaling laws for LLM continual pre-training [2]. There are also domain-specific curation methods for cultural seed discovery [8] and clinical synthetic data evaluation across fidelity, diversity, and privacy [10].
